```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

library(AlphaSimR)
```

## Why use miscellaneous data slots?

`AlphaSimR` generates a lot of information about each individual,
such as genome, genetic values, phenotypes, sex, etc.
This information is stored in slots of the `Pop` object,
and can be accessed via the `@` operator (say, `pop@gv`) or
some accessor functions (say, `gv(pop)`).

Sometimes we may want to store additional information
beyond these standard `Pop` slots.
For example, we may want to store covariates, factor levels, or
other metadata for the individuals in a `Pop` object.
We may want to also store a summary of a `Pop` object.
While we can achieve all this by creating objects in the working environment,
it is convenient to keep the additional information in the `Pop` object itself.
This is what the `misc` and `miscPop` slots are for.

We use the `misc` slot for **individual miscellaneous data**.
This slot is a list.
Each list element must have one item per individual,
or one row of a matrix per individual,
both in the same order as individuals are stored in the `Pop` object.
We use the `miscPop` slot for **population miscellaneous data**.
This slot is also a list.
Both slots are empty and users can add data to them as shown below.

```{r create}
founders = quickHaplo(nInd=4, nChr=1, segSites=10)
SP = SimParam$new(founders)
pop = newPop(founders, simParam=SP)

pop@misc$cost = c(2, 4, 6, 8)
pop@misc$group = c("A", "A", "B", "B")
pop@misc$mat = matrix(rnorm(8), nrow=4, ncol=2)
pop@miscPop = list(totalCost=sum(pop@misc$cost),
                   groupCounts=table(pop@misc$group))
pop@misc
pop@miscPop
```

Because `list` is a flexible data structure,
we can store different types of objects in list elements of `misc` and `miscPop`.
Which types of objects are appropriate depends on the context,
but also if we can define a sensible behavior for these objects
when we are subsetting and merging populations.
This is explained in the next section.

## What happens by default when we subset or merge populations?

Subsetting a population **keeps `misc`** slot aligned with the individuals.
This is achieved by the default `subsetMisc()` function,
which is called by the subsetting operator.
This function knows how to subset `Pop` objects
(say, `pop@misc$otherPop[i]` - useful for mtDNA simulations),
matrices (say, `pop@misc$mat[i, , drop = FALSE]`), or
any type of vector-like object that can be subsetted with the `[` method (say, `pop@misc$obj[i]`).
However, subsetting a population **clears `miscPop`**.

```{r default-subset}
selected = pop[c(4, 2, 2)]
selected@misc
selected@miscPop
```

Merging populations combines their corresponding `misc` slots,
using `c()` for vector-like objects aand `rbind()` for matrices.
However, merging populations **clears `miscPop`**.

```{r default-merge}
combined = mergePops(list(pop, pop))
combined@misc
combined@miscPop
```

If the number or names of `misc` elements differ between populations,
the default merge function warns and clears **the entire `misc` slot**.
Use the same names in the same order to avoid this.

```{r incompatible-misc}
other = pop
other@misc$group = NULL
str(pop)
str(other)
combined = mergePops(list(pop, other))
combined@misc
```

Subsetting and merging populations clears the `miscPop`
because it is not clear how to recompute the information.
This can be customized with user defined functions,
as described in the next section.

## Customize the behavior with user-defined functions (hooks)

Four independent functions (hooks) saved in `SimParam`
control the subset and merge operations with `misc` and `miscPop`.

| Function (hook) | Returns |
|:---|:---|
| `SP$subsetMisc` | `misc` for a subset |
| `SP$subsetMiscPop` | `miscPop` for a subset |
| `SP$mergeMisc` | `misc` for a merged population |
| `SP$mergeMiscPop` | `miscPop` for a merged population |

Each function returns a list for its own slot.
Subset functions receive the original `pop` and index `i`.
Merge functions receive the original populations as `popList`, in merge order.
By storing these functions into the `SimParam` object,
they are used by the subsetting and merging operators.
We can pass this `SimParam` object explicitly to the operators, or
we can rely on the global `SimParam` object named `SP` if available.

For example, to recompute the total cost whenever individuals are subsetted
or populations are merged you could use:

```{r population-functions}
SP$subsetMiscPop = function(pop, i, simParam=NULL){
  list(totalCost=sum(pop@misc$cost[i]))
}
SP$mergeMiscPop = function(popList, simParam=NULL){
  list(totalCost=sum(vapply(popList, function(pop) sum(pop@misc$cost), numeric(1))))
}

selected = pop[c(4, 2, 2)]
selected@miscPop
combined = c(pop, selected)
combined@miscPop
```

These functions also apply to populations created before the functions were set.
With the above two functions,
the individual data in `misc` still follow the default handling.
To customize subsetting and merging of `misc` too,
you could rewrite the default functions,
or call the exported default helpers inside a function and
then adjust their result.
Here we keep a record of the most recent operation for each individual:

```{r individual-functions}
SP$subsetMisc = function(pop, i, simParam=NULL){
  out = subsetMisc(pop, i, simParam=simParam)
  out$operation = rep("subset", length(out[[1]]))
  out
}
SP$mergeMisc = function(popList, simParam=NULL){
  out = mergeMisc(popList, simParam=simParam)
  out$operation = rep("merge", length(out[[1]]))
  out
}

left = pop[1:2]
right = pop[3:4]
left@misc$operation
combined = mergePops(list(left, right))
combined@misc$operation
combined@miscPop
```

Both functions for an operation see the original inputs.
A `miscPop` function does not see the result of the `misc` functions.
Ensure you use `subsetMisc()` inside a subset function rather than `pop[i]`,
which would call the function recursively indefinitely.
Note that the custom `misc` results must still have one item or
matrix row per resulting individual.

To restore the default behavior set any function to `NULL`

```{r reset-functions}
SP$subsetMisc = NULL
SP$mergeMisc = NULL
SP$subsetMiscPop = NULL
SP$mergeMiscPop = NULL
pop[1:2]@miscPop # list() again
```

See `?subsetMisc` for the function (hook) interface and defaults,
including `mergeMisc()`, `subsetMiscPop()` and `mergeMiscPop()`.
